hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast thrift stores house cats during Palm City shelter renovation
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is housing cats at its two thrift stores while the Palm City shelter undergoes construction on adoption, customer service, and intake areas.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is finding creative solutions to keep its animal care operations running smoothly while undergoing major renovations at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit began construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, which temporarily made many of the shelter's cages unavailable. To address this challenge, the organization has relocated many of its cats to its two thrift store locations throughout the renovation period.

According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, the thrift stores have become essential spaces for housing animals during construction. "With our shelter cages unavailable, the stores have become a lifeline for our animals," Fisher explained. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis added that shoppers visiting either thrift store can now browse merchandise while also meeting adoptable cats. This dual-purpose approach allows the organization to continue its adoption efforts while maintaining its retail operations that support the animals' care.

The presence of adoptable cats in the thrift stores offers an unexpected benefit to the community. Ellis emphasized that purchases made at the stores directly support animal care. "Every treasure you find here helps provide for our animals," she noted. The organization welcomes donations of gently used goods from the community, which helps sustain operations during the construction period. Additionally, the Humane Society is actively seeking temporary foster homes for other animals while the renovation work continues at the main facility.

The thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st Street in Stuart. Community members interested in adopting a cat, shopping for treasured items, donating goods, or becoming a temporary foster can visit either location. More information about store hours and donation guidelines is available at hstc1.org. The solution demonstrates how local animal welfare organizations can adapt to challenges while maintaining both their adoption programs and community connections during facility improvements.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax ballot language as biased and misleading
cards.teaser: A voter advocacy group and two registered voters filed a lawsuit Thursday challenging the property tax amendment language that Florida lawmakers approved for the November ballot.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the ballot language for a property-tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November 2026 General Election. The complaint, filed by a voter advocacy group and two registered voters, argues the ballot language is "biased" and "misleading," accusing lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases like "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs contend the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

Attorney Jamie Cole, representing the plaintiffs, argues that accurate wording matters because many voters will not study the full legal text before casting a ballot. Cole successfully challenged a similar property-tax amendment in 2007, when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed "Super Exemption" misleading and ordered the measure removed from the ballot. On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation to raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and create a framework for full exemption over time. The amendment will require approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police drone locates missing autistic woman on first day of new program
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie's Drone as First Responder program proved its value on its first day of testing Wednesday, completing 17 missions and locating a missing autistic woman before she could enter a body of water. Police received a report of an autistic female walking through a wooded area near a canal bank. A DFR drone was remotely deployed and arrived at the scene before responding officers, quickly locating both the missing woman and the reporting party. Drone operators maintained visual contact and directed responding officers to their exact location, allowing officers to safely reunite the woman with her family. The drones also responded to a burglary in progress where they provided aerial overwatch, a domestic violence investigation where the drone located a suspect in a backyard before patrol officers arrived, and multiple disturbance calls involving groups of minors.

The DFR program integrates directly with the department's computer-aided dispatch system, allowing trained personnel to remotely deploy drones from the police department before officers arrive. Drones can reach calls within seconds, with the longest travel time in the coverage area approximately four minutes. The program currently consists of 12 specially trained officers, with three drone docks installed and active during the testing phase. Once fully operational, six docks will be strategically placed throughout Port St. Lucie. Each drone has an average flight time of 25 to 35 minutes depending on weather conditions and provides real-time situational awareness to responding officers.

cards.headline: Wrongful death lawsuit filed in fatal Florida Turnpike crash that killed three in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Thursday months after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike near Mile Marker 171 in St. Lucie County that killed three people when a semi-truck driver made an illegal U-turn.
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Thursday months after a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike that killed three people when a semi-truck driver made an illegal U-turn in St. Lucie County. The lawsuit, filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph, names multiple defendants including truck driver Harjinder Singh, trucking company White Hawk Carriers Inc., freight broker C.H. Robinson, and company manager Harpreet Singh. On Aug. 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., Singh attempted an illegal U-turn through a median crossover near Mile Marker 171. The crossover was clearly marked "U-TURN OFFICIAL USE ONLY." The 53-foot trailer swung across and completely blocked all northbound travel lanes. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne, carrying passengers Rodrigue Dor and Faniola Joseph, struck the left side of the trailer in what the complaint describes as "a classic and fatal underride crash." All three occupants were killed, with Joseph pronounced dead at the scene.

The lawsuit alleges Singh was present in the United States illegally without lawful immigration status or work authorization, yet obtained a Class A California commercial driver's license in violation of federal and state regulations. Before C.H. Robinson selected White Hawk Carriers to transport the load, the trucking company had a documented unsafe federal safety record including a prior crash on approximately Dec. 9, 2024, roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations, repeated hours-of-service violations with falsified duty status records, and vehicle defects including brake problems and air-brake leaks. The lawsuit seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie fans travel to Boca Raton for Curaçao World Cup training ahead of historic debut
cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to witness Curaçao's team prepare for its first-ever World Cup appe.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday with jerseys and flags in hand to witness Curaçao's first-ever World Cup appearance. The team, known as the "Blue Wave," held a training session that drew enthusiastic supporters eager to see their favorite players ahead of the historic debut. Goalkeeper Eloy Room said the outpouring of support fueled the team's excitement. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today — it gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches.

Some Curaçao natives made the drive from as far as Port St. Lucie to attend the training event. Marionella Barzeycoggins, who is originally from Curaçao, said she made sure her whole family was there. "I found out they're gonna be in Boca and they have a training event. And I'm like, oh my God, I have to RSVP so we are here. I'm super excited about that and I'm able to bring my whole family," Barzeycoggins said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong said the moment carries enormous meaning for the entire island. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas.

State Representative Randy Fine canceled his appearance at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown after party officials announced gubernatorial candidate James Fishback would speak at the event. Fine, who is Jewish, posted on social media that he would not attend if the Florida GOP hosts what he called a Neo-Nazi rally. Fishback has gained attention for making openly racist attacks against frontrunner Byron Donalds and denying entry to Jewish students at an event at the University of South Florida earlier this year.

Fine had been announced as a featured guest before the party expanded its guest list Thursday to include several gubernatorial candidates. In addition to Fishback and Donalds, speakers include Lieutenant Governor candidate Jay Collins, former state House Speaker Paul Renner, and hunter Bobby Williams. The Republican Party recently announced that only Donalds had met polling requirements to appear at a debate at the event, but subsequently offered speaking slots to multiple candidates. Fishback and Fine have had public conflicts, with Fishback quoting Fine's pro-Israel positions during an interview with podcaster Tucker Carlson. Fine has called Carlson the most dangerous antisemite in the country. Fine also canceled an appearance with the Heritage Foundation when leaders refused to distance themselves from white nationalist Nick Fuentes, a figure Fishback has repeatedly praised. When asked about Fine's cancellation, Fishback texted Florida Politics saying good riddance.

cards.headline: Indian River County rents average $1,222 for one-bedroom, new federal data shows
cards.teaser: Indian River County residents pay an average of $1,222 monthly for one-bedroom apartments, according to new 2026 Fair Market Rent data released Thursday by the .
cards.body:
Indian River County residents pay an average of $1,222 monthly for one-bedroom apartments, according to new 2026 Fair Market Rent data released by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The figures place Indian River County in the middle range of South Florida rental costs. Belle Glade in Palm Beach County offers the lowest rents at $890 for one-bedroom units, while Wellington in the same county posts the highest rates at $2,850. Okeechobee County averages $1,032, and the St. Lucie and Martin County areas average $1,467. Real estate broker Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, attributes Wellington's high costs to quality amenities and location advantages, noting that school districts and lifestyle factors drive rental price differences. He identified the priciest rental markets in Wellington, western Lake Worth, Delray Beach and Boca Raton, and observed that more acreage and more land have become more popular even in the rental market.

Luis Rivera, a Section 8 housing resident in Palm Beach County, described the local rental market as difficult. "I was seeing over two, three grand and it wasn't even in reasonable neighborhoods," Rivera said. "When I first came down here rent prices were normal. And now it's like they're pushing us out." HUD's Fair Market Rent data reflects current market rates based on similar properties in each area, using surveys, rental listings, and market adjustments. The figures help calculate housing assistance programs but do not set rent control limits for landlords. The data provides insight for renters, policymakers, and housing advocates working to address regional affordability challenges.

cards.headline: Hundreds of dead fish found in Port St. Lucie neighborhood after city algae treatment
cards.teaser: Hundreds of dead fish floated in the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St.
cards.body:
Dead fish floated on the water at the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday following an algae treatment earlier in the week. Neighbors shared video of dead fish they found in their backyards Thursday morning. On Tuesday and Wednesday, the city hired SOLitude to treat the water for algae. Experts say that with high heat and algae treatment, the water can become uninhabitable for aquatic life. Neighbor Jim Herbert said there were hundreds and hundreds of fish just gulping for air. Another resident, Jerry Cook, said he does not think the problem is an overnight fix or even a couple months fix, but rather a few years fix.

On Thursday, city crews removed the dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water. This is at least the second time since Jim Herbert has lived in the neighborhood that there has been a fish die-off. Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, recommended the city look at more natural solutions, including planting aquatic vegetation, reducing the use of fertilizer, and removing sediment that can fuel algae growth. Moir said the city will end up in a cycle it cannot break unless it goes back to square one and starts with natural remediation.

cards.headline: Sara Baxter drops congressional bid and reenters Palm Beach County Commission race after Trump post
cards.teaser: Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he would prefer she remain on the commission.
cards.body:
Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he would prefer she remain on the commission. Baxter confirmed the decision exclusively to WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman, saying her initial run for Congress was motivated by her desire to help more people in her community. "With this new district and living in it, it was kind of one of those lifetime opportunities," Baxter said. "I want to be able to help residents and help more of them."

In a statement to Hoffman on Thursday night, Baxter said she had just spoken with President Donald Trump on the phone and was grateful for his tremendous leadership. Trump, who had previously endorsed Baxter's campaign to stay on the county commission, posted on Truth Social Thursday night saying he would rather have her remain on the commission than run for Congress. "Sara Baxter is a fantastic person, and highly qualified for many top political jobs but, on a somewhat selfish basis, I would rather have her stay on the Palm Beach County Commission (where so many important things are happening!), than run for Congress," Trump said. Political analyst Brian Crowley said that without Trump's endorsement for Baxter's congressional run, the race would be an uphill battle.

cards.headline: Fresh produce prices force Palm Beach County families to adapt shopping habits
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6 percent over the past year.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing their grocery buying habits as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and a new study from financial services company Advance America. One in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20% have switched to frozen alternatives. One Palm Beach County shopper who switched to frozen produce said the quality remains the same, noting that "you can get organic and all those things for quite the same price that you would find fresh." Another resident described his new shopping strategy: "I hit all these, there's a Don Victor's down in Lake Worth. It's a great place to get vegetables, so I just usually get them there. My shopping day consists of two or three stops now."

Not all consumers are dramatically altering their habits. Another shopper said prices have gone up but remain manageable for her since she shops only for one person and buys fresh produce in moderate quantities. The Advance America study found Florida residents now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods. Federal data shows overall grocery prices increased 2.7% year-over-year through May, with fresh produce leading the increases at more than 6%.

Drones can reach calls within seconds, with the longest travel time in the coverage area approximately four minutes. The program currently consists of 12 specially trained officers, with three drone docks installed and active during the testing phase. Once fully operational, six docks will be strategically placed throughout Port St. Lucie. Each drone has an average flight time of 25 to 35 minutes depending on weather conditions and provides real-time situational awareness to responding officers.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax ballot language as biased and misleading
cards.teaser: A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the property tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November ballot, arguing the ballot language is biased and misleading.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the property tax amendment Florida lawmakers approved for the November ballot, arguing the ballot language is biased and misleading. The complaint, filed by a voter advocacy group and two registered voters, accuses lawmakers of using campaign-style phrases such as "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes," "protecting small businesses" and "ensuring fairness." The plaintiffs contend the summary overstates the proposal by suggesting it guarantees funding for core services, fully eliminates non-school homestead taxes and immediately exempts the first $250,000 of a home's value, when the actual initial exemption would be $150,000 in 2027. The lawsuit asks a judge to declare the wording unconstitutional and order Attorney General James Uthmeier to rewrite it within 10 days.

Attorney Jamie Cole, representing the plaintiffs, argues the wording resembles political advertising rather than a neutral summary. Cole successfully challenged a similar property tax amendment in 2007, when a judge found the ballot language for a proposed "Super Exemption" misleading and removed it from the ballot. On June 2, lawmakers passed legislation raising the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, creating a framework for full exemption over time. The amendment will appear on the November 2026 General Election Ballot and requires approval from at least 60 percent of voters to become law.

hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast thrift stores house cats during Palm City shelter renovation
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is housing cats at its two thrift stores while the Palm City shelter undergoes construction on adoption, customer service, and intake areas.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is finding creative solutions to keep its animal care operations running smoothly while undergoing major renovations at its Palm City shelter. The nonprofit began construction on its adoption, customer service, and intake areas earlier this year, which temporarily made many of the shelter's cages unavailable. To address this challenge, the organization has relocated many of its cats to its two thrift store locations throughout the renovation period.

According to spokesperson Sarah Fisher, the thrift stores have become essential spaces for housing animals during construction. "With our shelter cages unavailable, the stores have become a lifeline for our animals," Fisher explained. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis added that shoppers visiting either thrift store can now browse merchandise while also meeting adoptable cats. This dual-purpose approach allows the organization to continue its adoption efforts while maintaining its retail operations that support the animals' care.

The presence of adoptable cats in the thrift stores offers an unexpected benefit to the community. Ellis emphasized that purchases made at the stores directly support animal care. "Every treasure you find here helps provide for our animals," she noted. The organization welcomes donations of gently used goods from the community, which helps sustain operations during the construction period. Additionally, the Humane Society is actively seeking temporary foster homes for other animals while the renovation work continues at the main facility.

The thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st Street in Stuart. Community members interested in adopting a cat, shopping for treasured items, donating goods, or becoming a temporary foster can visit either location. More information about store hours and donation guidelines is available at hstc1.org. The solution demonstrates how local animal welfare organizations can adapt to challenges while maintaining both their adoption programs and community connections during facility improvements.

cards.headline: Hundreds of dead fish found in Port St. Lucie community after city algae treatment
cards.teaser: Hundreds of dead fish were found floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St.
cards.body:
Dead fish were floating in the Sawgrass Lakes community in Port St. Lucie on Thursday after the city hired SOLitude to treat the water for algae on Tuesday and Wednesday. Neighbors shared videos with WPTV showing dead fish in their backyards Thursday morning. Resident Jim Herbert said hundreds of fish were gulping for air. Experts told WPTV that high heat combined with algae treatment can make water uninhabitable for aquatic life. On Thursday, crews removed the dead fish and tested oxygen levels in the water. Herbert said this is at least the second fish die-off since he has lived in the area.

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the city has been working with neighbors and other cities and counties to find solutions and is hoping options might be available soon, though those depend on several factors. Jim Moir, executive director of the Indian Riverkeeper, recommended the city pursue more natural solutions, including planting aquatic vegetation, reducing fertilizer use, and removing sediment that fuels algae growth. Moir said the city will remain stuck in a cycle unless it returns to square one and starts with natural remediation. The city has not announced when oxygen levels will return to normal or what specific steps will be taken to prevent future fish die-offs.

cards.headline: Corpse flower nicknamed Princess Pungent nearing bloom at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A rare Titan Arum, known as the corpse flower, could bloom within days or weeks at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach, emitting a stench of rotting flesh during its brief 24 to 48 hour bloom.
cards.body:
The rare Titan Arum, also known as the corpse flower and nicknamed "Princess Pungent," is set to bloom soon at McKee Botanical Garden in Vero Beach. According to the garden's Instagram account, which has been tracking the flower's progress, it could bloom within the next few days or weeks. During its bloom period, which typically lasts only 24 to 48 hours, the flower emits the stench of rotting flesh. The plant is native to the rainforests of Sumatra and Indonesia and is considered endangered.

This particular Titan Arum arrived at McKee in May 2026. In a Thursday update, the botanical garden reported that the flower has grown nine inches taller, and one of its three remaining leaves has dropped, signs that bloom time is approaching. McKee Botanical Garden's annual Waterlily Celebration takes place June 13, which means visitors may have the opportunity to see and smell the full bloom during the event.

cards.headline: Indian River County Fair Market Rent reaches $1,222 for one-bedroom apartments
cards.teaser: Indian River County's Fair Market Rent for a one-bedroom apartment reached $1,222, according to new 2026 data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
cards.body:
Indian River County posted a Fair Market Rent of $1,222 for one-bedroom apartments in 2026, according to new data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The figure places Indian River County between Okeechobee County at $1,032 and St. Lucie and Martin areas at $1,467 for comparable housing. HUD's Fair Market Rent reflects current market rates based on similar properties in each area, using surveys, rental listings and market adjustments.

Real estate broker Talbot Sutter, president of Sutter and Nugent Real Estate, recommends that renters conduct thorough research before committing to a lease. "Know the market, do your comps. You have to really, really know the area if you don't want to get ripped off paying rent," Sutter said. HUD's Fair Market Rent data provides crucial insight for renters, policymakers and housing advocates working to address regional affordability gaps.

cards.headline: St. Lucie and Martin area Fair Market Rent for one-bedroom apartments reaches $1,467
cards.teaser: Fair Market Rent in the St. Lucie and Martin areas reached $1,467 for one-bedroom apartments in 2026, according to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development data.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie and Martin areas posted Fair Market Rent of $1,467 for one-bedroom apartments in 2026, according to new data from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The figures reflect current market rates based on similar properties in each area, using surveys, rental listings and market adjustments. HUD's Fair Market Rent data helps calculate housing assistance programs but does not set rent control limits for landlords.

Luis Rivera, who lives in Section 8 housing in Palm Beach County, describes the local rental market simply: "It's not easy here." Rivera said he was seeing over two or three thousand dollars in rent and it wasn't even in reasonable neighborhoods. "When I first came down here rent prices were normal. And now it's like they're pushing us out," Rivera said. South Florida's rental market continues reflecting broader housing affordability challenges as residents balance income growth against rapidly rising living costs.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges Florida property tax ballot language as biased and misleading
cards.teaser: A lawsuit filed Thursday in Leon County challenges the property tax amendment approved by Florida lawmakers for the November ballot, arguing the language is biased and misleading with campaign-style phrases.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County families switch to frozen produce as fresh prices climb more than 6 percent
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6 percent over the past year, with one in three American families now purchasing fewer fresh fruits and vegetables.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing how they buy groceries as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6 percent over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and new consumer research. One in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20 percent have switched to frozen alternatives, according to a study from financial services company Advance America. One Palm Beach County shopper explained the switch to frozen produce, saying the quality remains the same and organic frozen options cost about as much as fresh alternatives.

Some shoppers are expanding their grocery routines to find better deals on fresh produce. One Palm Beach County resident described his new approach, noting that Don Victor's down in Lake Worth is a great place to get vegetables and that his shopping day now consists of two or three stops. The Advance America study found Florida residents now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods. Federal data shows overall grocery prices increased 2.7 percent year-over-year through May, with fresh produce leading the increases at more than 6 percent.

hero.headline: Wellington Soccer Club sees record 840 registrations as World Cup excitement builds
hero.teaser: More than 840 children have registered to play with the Wellington Soccer Club for the upcoming season, a record turnout that coaches and organizers attribute to growing World Cup excitement across South Florida.
hero.body:
The Wellington Soccer Club is experiencing unprecedented growth, with more than 840 children registering for the upcoming season. Club officials and coaches attribute this record-breaking turnout to increased enthusiasm surrounding the World Cup across South Florida. The surge reflects a pattern that emerges every four years when the international tournament captures public attention and inspires young athletes to pursue the sport.

At Greenview Shores Park, young players are training with professional aspirations in mind. Nine-year-old Parker exemplifies the motivation driving many of the club's new registrations. "I want to be like Allende when I grow up, he's my favorite player," Parker said. His inspiration is Tadeo Allende, an Argentinian soccer player who currently plays for Inter Miami. Having access to world-class talent in the local area has intensified interest in soccer among South Florida's youth.

Patrick Zoete, the club's director of coaching, brings more than 25 years of experience to his role. He emphasizes that soccer's appeal extends far beyond competitive athletics. "Soccer provides not only exercise but also a way of life for the kids to be part of a team, camaraderie. Some of them remain friends for life," Zoete said. He acknowledges the four-year cycle of increased interest tied to the World Cup schedule. "We wait four years for a World Cup. I mean, it's huge," Zoete said. "We're fortunate that we have Messi here at Inter Miami. We can go watch the best player in the world." The presence of international soccer stars playing in South Florida has made the sport more accessible and tangible for aspiring young players.

While major sporting events clearly drive registration numbers, young players cite deeper reasons for their commitment to the sport. Parker describes his primary motivation simply: "Spending time with my friends. I meet new people every year. Every time we have a game, I'm really excited." This sentiment reflects what keeps many children engaged season after season beyond the initial excitement of watching professional soccer. The Wellington Soccer Club is one of several organizations across the region experiencing similar registration spikes as the World Cup approaches, demonstrating the tournament's broad impact on youth sports participation in South Florida.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie fans travel to Boca Raton for Curaçao World Cup training ahead of historic debut
cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to witness Curaçao's team prepare for its first-ever World Cup appe.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday with jerseys and flags in hand to witness Curaçao's first-ever World Cup appearance. The team, known as the "Blue Wave," held a training session that drew enthusiastic supporters eager to see their favorite players ahead of the historic debut. Goalkeeper Eloy Room said the outpouring of support fueled the team's excitement. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today — it gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said. Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches.

Some Curaçao natives made the drive from as far as Port St. Lucie to attend the training event. Marionella Barzeycoggins, who is originally from Curaçao, said she made sure her whole family was there. "I found out they're gonna be in Boca and they have a training event. And I'm like, oh my God, I have to RSVP so we are here. I'm super excited about that and I'm able to bring my whole family," Barzeycoggins said. Midfielder Tahitch Chong said the moment carries enormous meaning for the entire island. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas.

cards.headline: Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves see roster numbers grow under new head coach Mike Colee
cards.teaser: The Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves are back on the gridiron, looking to prove themselves under new leadership as roster numbers climb under new head football coach Mike Colee.
cards.body:
Newly named head football coach Mike Colee is already making an impact on the Oxbridge Academy Thunderwolves program just a few weeks into his position. The roster numbers have grown since his arrival, after starting lower when he first took over. "It was a little bit lower numbers at the beginning," Colee said. "Everyone kind of made their plans for the summertime before I was really involved. But once I got in there, once I got to meet with the parents, meet with the kids, get the schedule out there, we've been growing our numbers ever since."

As the season approaches, players are responding positively to Colee's coaching approach. Senior Cayden Pribramski said the coach emphasizes mental toughness and plays to each player's strengths. "He's not the kind of guy to go out there and say, 'my way or the highway,'" Pribramski said. "He's going to really build the stuff around you and help you to succeed. So, I think that's going to be instrumental in our success as a team and our future success as a program as a whole." The Thunderwolves are focused on moving forward after last year's 0-11 season. "We just want to keep working, keep going," senior Brady Basis said. "We came off a good spring win. Keep bringing that energy and build it in the next season."

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast thrift stores in Stuart house adoptable cats during Palm City shelter renovation

Shoppers visiting either thrift store can now browse both merchandise and adoptable cats. Senior Manager Kelly Ellis encouraged customers to support the animals through their purchases. "Every treasure you find here helps provide for our animals," Ellis said, noting that donations of gently used goods are welcome. The Humane Society is also seeking temporary foster homes for other animals while construction continues. The thrift stores are located at 3302 SE Federal Highway in Stuart and 1099 NW 21st St, Stuart. Store hours and donation guidelines are available at hstc1.org.

cards.headline: Singer Island beach littered with trash and overflowing cans after Memorial Day
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach officials say beach staff worked throughout Memorial Day weekend to maintain the beach near Johnny Longboats, but higher-than-normal holiday attendance resulted in more trash than usual.
cards.body:
WPTV found Singer Island beach littered with overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans just feet away from sea turtle nests following Memorial Day weekend. Beachgoer Stacie Safford expressed concern for the environment and nesting sea turtles. "I am seeing the same thing you are seeing. A whole lot of garbage," Safford said.

The city of Riviera Beach said higher-than-normal holiday attendance resulted in significantly increased beach activity and more trash than usual. Beach maintenance staff were scheduled starting at 7 a.m. over the weekend, with Memorial Day coverage beginning at 6:30 a.m. The city increased beach restroom cleanings to three times during the weekend, including Monday, up from the usual two weekend cleanings. The city noted that during turtle season, sifting and combing are permitted only in limited beach areas to protect sea turtle nests. Oceanside Beach Services assists with trash removal and seaweed clearing in designated areas, while vendors and turtle volunteers help protect nests. Safford urged visitors to be more mindful. "This isn't the first time I have seen the trash cans overflowing, take your trash with you, throw it out, even if the cans are full," she said.

hero.headline: Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square in Delray Beach opens upcycled art exhibition through September
hero.teaser: The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened its newest summer exhibition, Persistence of Matter, spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into striking works of art.
hero.body:
The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened its newest summer exhibition, Persistence of Matter, spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into striking works of art. According to Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority Cultural Arts Director Marusca Gatto, the show underscores the museum's mission to marry creativity with community impact. Guest curators Mavis Benson and Pamela Lambie have selected artists whose sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces are all crafted from reclaimed objects. Featured creators include Autumn Kioti, whose work draws on natural and urban influences, and Mike Silverman, whose Self-Reflection series uses discarded hard drive platters and printed circuit boards to create reflective sculptures. "Every piece invites viewers to see themselves and their relationship to technology and waste in a new light," Silverman said.

The exhibition runs through Sept. 10, 2026, with special programs including artist talks, salon discussions, and film screenings. Museum hours are Wednesday from noon to 5 p.m., Thursday and Friday from noon to 7 p.m., Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. For event details, call 561-654-2220.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Public Library offers free STREAM summer programs with daily lunches for Florida youth
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Public Library is making summer brighter for kids and teens with free STREAM programs covering Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math, open to all Florida residents.
cards.body:
The Delray Beach Public Library is offering free STREAM summer programs—Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math—to all Florida residents. Young adult librarian Natalie Baron leads sessions including ColorSpace: Artistic Excavations, where teens explore art history from cave paintings to ancient pottery. Participants can engage in collaborative 3D puzzle builds and select themed book boxes. Children's department head Mandy Fulop is launching the STREAM Into Summer Literacy Program, which encourages young readers to set goals with librarians, track progress, and take home an Unearth a Story bag containing a free STREAM book and related activities. Registration is available at delraylibrary.org.

In partnership with the School District of Palm Beach County, the library serves free lunch daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and snacks from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. for youth up to 18 years old. Family Nights on select Tuesdays invite children age 5 and older to explore STREAM topics together. Saturday Science Discovery programs for ages 9 through 12 feature hands-on archaeology activities including Piece Together History, trash bag archaeology, carbon dating, and fossil hunts. Upcoming Thursday guest speakers include Malachi Fenn from the Florida Public Archaeology Network on June 11, Sea Turtle Adventures beach cleanup on June 25, American Shark Conservancy's SharkSmarts on July 2, and FPAN Beyond Artifacts on July 16. For complete program details and registration, visit delraylibrary.org.

hero.headline: Florida Democratic Party Announces Leadership Blue Conference at Disney World in July
hero.teaser: The Florida Democratic Party will hold its annual Leadership Blue Weekend July 17-19 at Disney's Gran Destino Tower at Coronado Springs in Lake Buena Vista.
hero.body:
The Florida Democratic Party is preparing for its signature annual event as Leadership Blue Weekend returns to Central Florida next month. The conference will run July 17-19 at Disney's Gran Destino Tower at Coronado Springs Resort in Lake Buena Vista. The multiday gathering brings together candidates, activists, and party leaders to establish shared campaign priorities ahead of the 2026 election cycle. Sessions will include campaign training, policy discussions, strategy workshops, and networking opportunities designed to help Democrats prepare for the midterm elections. The event has historically functioned as a coordinating hub where Democratic campaigns, advocacy organizations, and party groups align efforts and build support before major statewide races.

The conference schedule culminates with the annual Leadership Blue Gala, the party's premier fundraising event. This gala provides Democratic candidates and organizations with a critical opportunity to connect with supporters and donors as the campaign season accelerates. Party officials have confirmed that prominent national leaders will participate in the event, though the complete speaker roster has not yet been revealed. Previous Leadership Blue conferences have included notable figures such as U.S. Senator Cory Booker and Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, establishing the event's track record of attracting high-profile Democratic voices.

The gala is anticipated to draw elected officials, major donors, grassroots activists, and national media attention. Democrats see this gathering as essential to rebuilding momentum in Florida ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The state has historically represented a challenging electoral landscape for the party in recent years, making the coordinated efforts fostered by Leadership Blue increasingly important to their strategic planning.

Interested attendees can access tickets and the full conference schedule through LeadershipBlue.com. The event represents a significant moment in the Democratic Party's 2026 electoral strategy, offering a structured opportunity for party members across different levels and roles to unify around shared campaign goals and messaging before heading into the election cycle.

cards.headline: Randy Fine Withdraws From Florida GOP Event After James Fishback Named Speaker
cards.teaser: State Representative Randy Fine canceled his appearance at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown after party officials announced Governor ca.
cards.body:
State Representative Randy Fine canceled his appearance at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown after party officials announced gubernatorial candidate James Fishback would speak at the event. Fine, who is Jewish, posted on social media that he would not attend if the Florida GOP hosts what he called a Neo-Nazi rally. Fishback has gained attention for making openly racist attacks against frontrunner Byron Donalds and denying entry to Jewish students at an event at the University of South Florida earlier this year.

Fine had been announced as a featured guest before the party expanded its guest list Thursday to include several gubernatorial candidates. In addition to Fishback and Donalds, speakers include Lieutenant Governor candidate Jay Collins, former state House Speaker Paul Renner, and hunter Bobby Williams. The Republican Party recently announced that only Donalds had met polling requirements to appear at a debate at the event, but subsequently offered speaking slots to multiple candidates. Fishback and Fine have had public conflicts, with Fishback quoting Fine's pro-Israel positions during an interview with podcaster Tucker Carlson. Fine has called Carlson the most dangerous antisemite in the country. Fine also canceled an appearance with the Heritage Foundation when leaders refused to distance themselves from white nationalist Nick Fuentes, a figure Fishback has repeatedly praised. When asked about Fine's cancellation, Fishback texted Florida Politics saying good riddance.

cards.headline: Orlando Marks 10th Anniversary of Pulse Nightclub Shooting That Killed 49
cards.teaser: Florida observes the 10th anniversary of the Pulse nightclub massacre, one of the deadliest mass shootings in American history.
cards.body:
On June 12, 2016, at 2:09 a.m., Omar Mateen of Port St. Lucie entered Pulse nightclub in Orlando armed with an AR-15-style rifle and a handgun and opened fire on nearly 300 people attending Latin Night. The attack continued for hours until about 5 a.m., when police used explosives to create a hole through a bathroom wall and shot and killed Mateen. By the time the attack ended, 49 people were dead, making it the deadliest mass shooting in the U.S. until one year later, when 58 people were murdered at a Las Vegas country music concert. Twenty-three of those killed were Puerto Rican. The attack devastated Orlando, communities across Florida, Puerto Rico and the nation.

Survivor Patience Murray was 20 years old when she attended Pulse with her best friend Tiara Parker and Parker's 18-year-old cousin, Akyra Murray. Murray was shot in both legs but survived. Akyra Murray was one of the 49 victims who did not make it out alive. Since the shooting, the old Pulse site was demolished in March. A permanent memorial is now 60 percent complete and expected to open by the end of 2027. It will feature a reflecting pool, a private gathering area, a healing garden, a survivors wall, and sealed capsules with personal items from the 49 victims.

cards.headline: Bill Mitchell Exits House District 60 Race, Endorses Melissa Rutland
cards.teaser: Trial attorney Bill Mitchell withdrew from the House District 60 race days after entering, throwing his support behind Republican Melissa Rutland.
cards.body:
Trial attorney Bill Mitchell will not run for Florida House District 60, announcing his decision Thursday after Republican Melissa Rutland entered the race with apparent support from House leadership. Mitchell had announced earlier in the week his intention to run for the seat being vacated by incumbent Democrat Lindsay Cross, saying he wanted to ensure an election would occur since only Democrat Lindsay Polega-Quigley had initially filed. Rutland's campaign treasurer is Noreen Fenner, an accountant associated with the Florida House Republican Campaign Committee. Pinellas County Tax Collector Adam Ross endorsed Rutland on Thursday, ahead of Mitchell's withdrawal announcement.

Mitchell told Florida Politics that since announcing his campaign, "the calls and support I have received have been overwhelming and humbling." After Rutland entered the race, he decided to step aside to support her, citing her "abundant support." He said he will "support Melissa" and plans "to campaign alongside her to flip HD 60." Mitchell is a partner at Gordon Rees Scully Mansukhani and a former Air Force aircraft mechanic turned civil trial attorney who served 15 years in the Air Force. He has lived in Feather Sound for 11 years and serves as President of the Feather Sound Community Services Board. Assuming no other candidates file before Friday's qualifying deadline, Rutland and Polega-Quigley will face each other in November. House District 60 is a swing district where Democrats outnumber Republicans by fewer than 1,000 out of more than 108,000 voters.

cards.headline: Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson Endorses Emily Duda Buckley for House District 38
cards.teaser: Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson endorsed Emily Duda Buckley in the race for House District 38, a potentially competitive open seat in Central Florida.
cards.body:
Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson is endorsing Emily Duda Buckley in her bid for Florida House District 38. Duda Buckley is one of three Republicans hoping to succeed David Smith, who cannot run again because of term limits. She and Marcus Hyatt have already qualified for the race, but Austyn Cydney Spell has not. Candidates have until Friday to qualify. Democrat Michelle Danielle DeJesus has filed to run as well. If she qualifies, the race will go to a General Election. If she does not, and no other Democrat joins, the winner will be decided in an open Republican Primary.

Simpson said Duda Buckley knows firsthand the challenges that hard-working families and business owners face and will tackle them with conservative values and tireless problem-solving. Duda Buckley said Simpson has spent his life standing up for Florida's farmers, families, and small businesses, and she is honored to have his support. House District 38 covers southwest Seminole County and includes Altamonte Springs, Casselberry, and Winter Springs. The constituency is about 34 percent Democratic and 33 percent Republican, with nearly 30 percent unaffiliated, according to L2 voter data. Smith won his last re-election by fewer than 700 votes against Democrat Sarah Henry. Duda Buckley has raised more than $215,000 through her campaign and political committee, Fostering Florida's Future. She grew up in Central Florida, attended Florida State University where she served as a Guardian Ad Litem, and later became a licensed foster parent working with the Florida Association of Foster and Adoptive Parents.

cards.headline: Florida Communities Hold Events to Honor Pulse Nightclub Victims 10 Years Later
cards.teaser: Businesses, churches, nonprofits and the city of Orlando are hosting special events and fundraisers Friday to remember the 49 victims of the Pulse nightclub massacre.
cards.body:
Friday marks the 10th anniversary of the Pulse nightclub massacre, and Orlando communities are gathering to remember the 49 victims through various events and tributes. OneBlood will host a blood drive beginning at 8 a.m. Friday at Orlando City Hall. The city is also offering a free exhibition called "Created in Community: Portraits of Pulse," featuring 49 portraits honoring those lost. Local artist Jeff Sonksen designed the portraits in a paint-by-number format, which were completed in 2017 by victims' families, friends, and community members. An outdoor ribbon exhibit displaying support Orlando received remains on display outside City Hall through June. The Pulse Memorial site will be illuminated nightly from dusk to dawn through June 15 as a peaceful visual tribute.

hero.headline: Wellington has highest rents in Palm Beach County while Belle Glade offers cheapest

hero.headline: C.H. Robinson named in St. Lucie County wrongful death lawsuit over fatal Turnpike crash
hero.teaser: C.H. Robinson Company Inc., one of the largest transportation brokers in the United States, is named as a defendant in the wrongful death lawsuit over the August 2025 Florida's Turnpike crash in St. Lucie County.
hero.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit filed in St. Lucie County names C.H. Robinson Company Inc., a major transportation broker based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, as a defendant in connection with a fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike. On August 12, 2025, at approximately 2:57 p.m., truck driver Harjinder Singh attempted an illegal U-turn through a median crossover near Mile Marker 171. The crossover was clearly marked "U-TURN OFFICIAL USE ONLY." As Singh's 53-foot trailer swung across the roadway, it completely blocked all northbound travel lanes. A minivan driven by Herby Dufresne struck the left side of the trailer in what the lawsuit describes as an underride crash. All three occupants of the minivan were killed, including Faniola Joseph, who was pronounced dead at the scene.

The lawsuit alleges that C.H. Robinson selected White Hawk Carriers Inc. despite the trucking company's documented safety problems. According to the complaint, White Hawk Carriers had a prior reportable crash in December 2024, multiple roadside inspection citations for unsafe driving violations including speeding and improper lane changes, repeated hours-of-service violations with falsified duty status records, and vehicle defects including brake problems and air-brake leaks. This safety information was publicly available through the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration's Safety Measurement System. The complaint contends that C.H. Robinson markets itself as a company that properly vets carriers using federal safety data but failed to adequately do so in this case.

The lawsuit also targets Harpreet Singh, identified as a White Hawk Carriers manager and California resident, claiming he was personally responsible for hiring, training, and supervising drivers including Harjinder Singh. The complaint alleges that Harpreet Singh failed to adequately investigate Harjinder Singh's immigration status, work authorization, English proficiency, and overall fitness before hiring. The lawsuit further alleges that Harjinder Singh was present in the United States illegally without lawful immigration status and without authorization to work. Despite this alleged status, Singh obtained a Class A California commercial driver's license, which the complaint states California issued in violation of applicable federal and state regulations. Additionally, the lawsuit claims Singh lacked required English language proficiency mandated under federal regulations.

At the time of the crash, an unauthorized passenger identified as Harneet Singh was in the truck cab, representing additional violations of safety standards and federal motor carrier regulations according to the complaint. The lawsuit was filed by an attorney representing the estate of victim Faniola Joseph and names multiple defendants including the truck driver, the trucking company, C.H. Robinson, and the company manager. The case seeks damages exceeding $75,000 under Florida's Wrongful Death Act, with Joseph's daughter entitled to compensation for her mother's death.

"I was seeing over two, three grand and it wasn't even in reasonable neighborhoods," Rivera said. "When I first came down here rent prices were normal. And now it's like they're pushing us out." HUD's Fair Market Rent data reflects current market rates based on similar properties in each area, using surveys, rental listings, and market adjustments. The figures help calculate housing assistance programs but do not set rent control limits for landlords. The data provides insight for renters, policymakers, and housing advocates working to address regional affordability challenges.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County families switch to frozen produce as fresh prices climb 6%
cards.teaser: Fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, prompting Palm Beach County shoppers to change how they buy groceries, according to Thursday's federal inflation report.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County shoppers are changing their grocery habits as fresh fruit and vegetable prices climbed more than 6% over the past year, according to Thursday's federal inflation report and a new study from financial services company Advance America. One in three American families now purchase fewer fresh fruits and vegetables due to rising costs, while 20% have switched to frozen alternatives. One Palm Beach County shopper who switched to frozen produce said the quality remains comparable, noting "you can get organic and all those things for quite the same price that you would find fresh."

Some shoppers are expanding their routines to find better deals. One Palm Beach County resident said his shopping day now consists of two or three stops, including Don Victor's in Lake Worth, which he described as "a great place to get vegetables." Not all consumers are dramatically altering their habits. Another shopper said prices have increased but remain manageable since she shops only for one person, and she continues buying fresh produce in moderate quantities. The Advance America study found Florida residents now spend over $28 more monthly on groceries compared to previous periods. Federal data shows overall grocery prices increased 2.7% year-over-year through May, with fresh produce leading increases at more than 6%.

cards.headline: Curaçao World Cup team holds training session in Boca Raton before historic debut
cards.teaser: Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to witness Curaçao's training session ahead of its first-ever World Cup appearance this weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of soccer fans filled Florida Atlantic University stadium in Boca Raton on Thursday to witness history as Curaçao prepared for its first-ever World Cup appearance. The team, known as the "Blue Wave," held a training session that drew enthusiastic supporters eager to catch a glimpse of their favorite players. Goalkeeper Eloy Room said the outpouring of support has fueled the team's excitement. "Really joyful to see that so many people showed up today. It gives us energy. We're really excited to start the World Cup," Room said.

Curaçao, an island nation with a population of just over 150,000 people, is the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament and went undefeated in all 10 of its 2026 World Cup qualifying matches. Midfielder Tahitch Chong told WPTV the moment carries enormous meaning for the entire island. "I think it's amazing to see. I don't think the people back home are going to believe the crowd we had here," Chong said. Fans traveled from across South Florida, with some Curaçao natives making the drive from as far as Port St. Lucie. Marionella Barzeycoggins, originally from Curaçao, brought her whole family after finding out about the training event. Curaçao faces Germany this Sunday in Houston, Texas.

cards.headline: Sara Baxter drops congressional bid, returns to Palm Beach County Commission race
cards.teaser: Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social Thursday night that he would prefer she remain on the commission.
cards.body:
Mayor Sara Baxter is dropping her congressional bid and reentering the Palm Beach County Commission race after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that he would prefer she remain on the commission. Baxter confirmed the decision exclusively to WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman, saying her initial run for Congress was motivated by her desire to help more people in her community. "With this new district and living in it, it was kind of one of those lifetime opportunities," Baxter said. In a statement to Hoffman on Thursday night, Baxter said she just had the honor of speaking with President Donald Trump on the phone. "I'm grateful for his tremendous leadership and I'm proud to consider him a true friend. There's more work ahead, and I'm ready to keep serving the people of Palm Beach County," she said.

Trump, who had previously endorsed Baxter's campaign to stay on the county commission, posted on Truth Social Thursday night expressing his preference that she remain on the commission rather than run for Congress. "Sara Baxter is a fantastic person, and highly qualified for many top political jobs but, on a somewhat selfish basis, I would rather have her stay on the Palm Beach County Commission (where so many important things are happening!), than run for Congress," Trump said. Political analyst Brian Crowley said that without Trump's endorsement for Baxter's congressional run, the race would be an uphill battle. "If he stays quiet, or if he endorses somebody else, it may make the hill that she has to climb even higher," Crowley said.
